- **Ground lenses** [`lenses`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lenses.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Burning crystals are a known curiosity (Aristophanes). Gem cutters polish rock crystal; glass is cast or core-formed, tinted and bubbly. Nobody grinds a lens to see with. Local: gem engravers and rock-crystal workers; Alpine rock crystal.
- **Spectacles** [`spectacles`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spectacles.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. The rich have slaves read aloud and take dictation, which blunts demand. A gem cutter can grind convex lenses from rock crystal; clear glass is the bottleneck.
- **Law of refraction, image formation and vision** [`refraction_optics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/refraction_optics.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Euclid's Optics: rays leave the eye. Epicureans (Lucretius, book 4) say thin films fly off things into it. The bent oar is a stock puzzle; no angles are measured. Local: Lucretius, De rerum natura (book 4); Euclid's Optics in Greek.
- **Camera obscura** [`camera_obscura`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/camera_obscura.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. The Aristotelian Problems note crescent suns under trees during an eclipse. A dark room with a small hole is an afternoon's work; nobody has made one.
- **Microscope** [`microscope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/microscope.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. A fused bead of very clear glass magnifies strongly, but glass here is tinted and bubbly and rock crystal cannot be fused. Physicians would scoff until shown.
- **Telescope (refractor)** [`telescope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/telescope.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept high. Needs two well-ground lenses of clear material; small rock-crystal ones are possible. No concave lens exists anywhere. Generals, ship captains and astronomers would pay.
- **Reflecting telescope** [`reflecting_telescope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reflecting_telescope.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Archimedes' On Floating Bodies exists in Greek, read by few. Shipwrights load by experience; nobody assays coin or bullion by weighing in water. Local: mint at the temple of Juno Moneta; money-changers (nummularii) who test coin by touch and sound.
- **Falling bodies and projectiles** [`falling_bodies`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/falling_bodies.md) — K1, use wrong, make easy, accept low. Aristotle: heavier falls faster. Lucretius (book 2) says all bodies would fall equally fast in a void, air and water alone slowing them. Nobody drops two weights to see. Local: Lucretius, De rerum natura (book 2).
- **Laws of motion** [`laws_of_motion`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/laws_of_motion.md) — K1, use wrong, make medium, accept low. Aristotle: motion needs a mover, the air pushes a thrown stone on. Epicurean atoms move forever through the void, a bridge to inertia.
- **Universal gravitation** [`universal_gravitation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_gravitation.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Heavy things seek the centre of the cosmos (Aristotle, Stoics). Needs laws of motion, elliptical orbits and algebra first.
- **Strength of materials and scaling** [`strength_of_materials`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/strength_of_materials.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Beams, arches and the new concrete vaults are sized by rule and experience. Catapult makers scale every part from the spring-hole diameter by Philo's formula. Local: Caesar's artillery engineers.
- **Sundial and water clock** [`sundial_water_clock`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sundial_water_clock.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Hours are twelfths of daylight, long in summer, short in winter. Courts time speeches by water clock. Rome's first public dial, booty from Catania, ran wrong for 99 years. Local: sundials by the Rostra in the Forum (Marcius Philippus' corrected dial, 164 BC); public water clock set up by Scipio Nasica (159 BC). Elsewhere: Athens: Tower of the Winds of Andronicus of Cyrrhus, sundials and a water clock; Alexandria: Ctesibius' regulated water clock (c. 270 BC).

Bronze gear trains exist in Greek planetary devices, but no escapement. Equal hours clash with the seasonal hours everyone lives by.
- **Pendulum clock** [`pendulum_clock`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pendulum_clock.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Needs a working escapement clock first. A bare pendulum for counting short times is easy and would serve physicians and astronomers.

Weather is read from star risings on peg calendars (parapegmata), birds and sky signs, as in Aratus. Rain gauge and wind vane are easy, a barometer is not. Educated Romans accept a globe with climate zones (Cicero's Dream of Scipio). Eratosthenes' 252,000 stadia competes with smaller figures from Posidonius. Nobody has sailed around it. Local: Cicero, De re publica (book 6). Elsewhere: Alexandria: Eratosthenes' Geography and measurement (c. 240 BC); Rhodes: school of Posidonius (died c. 51 BC).

Greek astronomy explains seasons by the Sun's tilted yearly circle around a resting Earth, obliquity about 24 degrees (Eratosthenes). A tilted, moving Earth is the new part.
- **Cause and prediction of eclipses** [`eclipse_prediction`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/eclipse_prediction.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. The educated know the cause: Gallus explained the lunar eclipse before Pydna (168 BC). For soldiers and plebs it is a prodigy. Prediction by cycles is Babylonian and Greek work. Elsewhere: Babylon: astronomical diaries and saros-cycle prediction; Rhodes and Alexandria: Hipparchus' lunar theory.
- **Heliocentric model** [`heliocentrism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heliocentrism.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. Aristarchus' hypothesis is known through Archimedes' Sand-Reckoner and rejected: no star shift is seen, and Cleanthes the Stoic called it impious. Only Seleucus defended it. Local: Greek copies of Archimedes' Sand-Reckoner.
